benefits: Enter any one measurement - radius, diameter, circumference, or area - and get the other three.
Perfect for craft, construction, and school geometry: pipe sizes, pizza areas, wheel distances.
Shows every formula it uses, so you learn the maths while you calculate.

faqs.a: Diameter = 2 x radius, so radius = diameter / 2. A 14 cm pizza has radius 7 cm. The tool does this the moment you switch the dropdown to Diameter.
faqs.q: How do I get the radius from the diameter?

faqs.a: Rearrange the circumference formula: r = C / (2 x pi). For a 44 cm wheel rim, r = 44 / 6.2832 = 7.0028, essentially 7 cm.
faqs.q: How do I find the radius from the circumference?

faqs.a: Rearrange the area formula: r = sqrt(A / pi). For a 154 cm2 circle, r = sqrt(154 / 3.14159) = sqrt(49.02) = 7.0014, essentially 7 cm.
faqs.q: How do I find the radius from the area?

faqs.a: Multiply the radius by 2 and by pi: C = 2 x pi x r. For r = 7, C = 43.9823. One full turn of a wheel with radius 7 cm rolls about 44 cm forward.
Yes. Enter the value in centimetres and all answers are in centimetres (area in cm2); enter inches and everything is in inches. Just never mix units in one calculation.
faqs.q: Does it work with inches or centimetres?

faqs.a: Pi is irrational, so the tool uses a high-precision value and displays 4 decimals. For r = 7 the area shows 153.938, true to 153.9380400... - plenty for any practical job.

circle-calculator.formula:
Diameter: d = 2r
Circumference: C = 2 x pi x r = pi x d
Area: A = pi x r squared
Reverse: r = d / 2 = C / (2 x pi) = sqrt(A / pi)
Example: r = 7 -> d = 14, C = 43.9823, A = 153.938
howTo: Choose which measurement you know: radius, diameter, circumference, or area.
Type its value - keep one unit for everything (all cm, or all inches).
The other three measurements appear instantly, to 4 decimal places.
Switch the dropdown any time to start from a different known value.
keyFacts: Radius 7 gives diameter 14, circumference 43.9823, and area 153.938.
Diameter is always exactly twice the radius: d = 2r.
Circumference = 2 x pi x r. One wheel turn rolls the wheel forward by its circumference.
Area = pi x r squared. Doubling the radius quadruples the area.
Any one of the four measurements determines the other three.
Pi here is precise enough that 4-decimal answers are correct for practical work.
